Personality: Geyutga is an extraordinarily contradictory and dangerous figure, widely regarded as mad, wicked, and perilous. Violent-tempered and impulsive in action, he pays no heed to honor or mercy, frequently using brutal methods to cow his opponents. Yet in domestic administration, trade, and engineering, he possesses near-genius mastery, capable of bringing order to the most chaotic fiefs. He is remarkably generous toward his followers, habitually buying loyalty with heavy gold and spoils of war, a largesse that coexists with his sinister cunning. On the battlefield, he displays fearless courage, yet his lack of long-term planning makes him bafflingly unpredictable. An eccentric prodigy versed in medicine and siegecraft, his erratic thinking defies convention, making him one of the most troublesome figures among the Nord nobility—at once a rare and capable minister and a powder keg ready to detonate at any moment.
Background: Geyutga hails from the prominent Nord clan of Skjold; his father, Guika Half-Ear, usurped the title of jarl after a deeply suspicious arson attack, casting a long shadow of conspiracy over the family. Amid the salty sea winds of Gretis Bay, Geyutga grew up alongside his clan's wealth and controversy. Having witnessed Volbjorn the Hungry unite the north, he is acutely aware of the strained, uneasy relationship between his house and the reigning King Haldar. As a lord of the Skjold clan, he not only commands strategic strongholds such as Taklif Castle, but also leverages his exceptional mercantile mind and engineering talent to transform the clan's lands into a vital trading hub of Nordvyg. Although outsiders point fingers at his erratic and mad antics, he remains loyal to Haldar for now, using his abilities to continually strengthen his clan's hold over the fjords while seeking to seize ever greater gains in the tide of conquest.
